She became the first Black artist to win Best Country Album and the first Black woman to win Album of the Year since [Lauryn Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauryn_Hill "Lauryn Hill") in [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/41st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "41st Annual Grammy Awards").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-6) [Chappell Roan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappell_Roan "Chappell Roan") took home [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), and [Sierra Ferrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Ferrell "Sierra Ferrell") swept the American roots categories, winning all four of her nominations.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-7) Best New Artist nominee [Doechii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doechii "Doechii") won [Best Rap Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Album "Best Rap Album") for _[Alligator Bites Never Heal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alligator_Bites_Never_Heal "Alligator Bites Never Heal"),_ becoming the third woman to win the award after Hill (with the [Fugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugees "Fugees")) in [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "39th Annual Grammy Awards") and [Cardi B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardi_B "Cardi B") in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards"). Other three-time winners included [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") and [St. Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Vincent_\(musician\) "St. Vincent \(musician\)").
